title: STA: root-cause analysis for microservice incidents
tagline: Ranks the service that caused a microservice incident from its metrics, and stays accurate as the system grows to hundreds of services.
problem: When a microservice system degrades, alerts fire on many services at once and on-call engineers lose time finding the one that started it. Graph models that look at every service pair get slower as the system grows.
approach: Select-Then-Analyze (STA) first scores every service cheaply and keeps the k most suspect ones, then runs a spatio-temporal graph network on that k-node subgraph only, so cost is O(N + k^2) instead of O(N^2) for dense full-graph analysis. The model ships as a self-describing bundle served by FastAPI, compared against the BARO statistical baseline on the same candidates.

demo.caption: docker-free local run: the FastAPI service ranks the services of a seeded synthetic Sock Shop incident via /predict, then the measured latency-vs-N chart of STA against full-graph models.

limits: All showcase numbers come from synthetic, seeded data; real-trace numbers (RCAEval) need the external dataset and are not regenerated here.
Latency is measured on CPU with untrained weights at batch 1; no GPU numbers.
STA's CPU latency is not flat: its O(N) selector dominates at batch 1 and a sparse full-graph GCN is O(E), so STA is slower than the GCN below N=2000.
BARO needs no training and ties STA on local crash faults; STA's gain is largest on cascading failures and at larger N.
